9	The scaling of LLMs toward long-context inference has shifted the primary serving

25	1 Introduction
26	The rapid scaling of LLM parameters and the growing demand for long-context inference shift
27	the bottleneck from computation to memory, where prefix KV cache management has become a
28	critical challenge in LLM serving [1]. As local GPU HBM and DRAM fall short of the TB-level
29	requirements of KV cache capacity, RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems emerge as the
30	standard solution for memory expansion and cross-node sharing [2–4].
31	In RDMA-based disaggregated systems, RDMA NICs prefetch the entire prefix KV cache into local
32	memory to ensure low-latency access during the subsequent decoding stages of the request. Although
33	this full fetching strategy is optimal fordense attentionmodels, it becomes fundamentally inefficient
34	for the emerging generation ofsparse attentionmodels, such as DeepSeek-V3.2 [ 5], GLM-5.1 [6]
35	and DeepSeek-V4 [7]. The core problem is that only a small fraction of KV entries are active at any
36	decoding step, while the KV cache for the full context must be fetched and remain in local memory
37	during the request. We find that the KV cache full fetching approach directly impacts the efficiency
38	of disaggregated serving systems for sparse attention models due to two primary problems.
39	(P1) Transmission Bottleneck.Due to the significantly reduced computational complexity, the
40	serving throughput of sparse attention models is typically bounded by the achievable batch size,
41	rather than the compute capacity [8]. For long-context requests, KV cache size can reach dozens of
42	GBs [9]. Maintaining high concurrency in sparse attention serving places substantial pressure on KV
43	cache transmission, including RDMA transfers and memory layout rearrangement, which can cause
44	long queuing delays and degrade time to first token and overall throughput.
45	*This work was done while the author was an intern at Alibaba Cloud.
46	Preprint.
47	arXiv:2606.19746v1  [cs.DC]  18 Jun 2026
48	
49	## PDF Page 2
50	
51	(P2) Local Memory Wasting.In sparse attention architectures, only the top-k KV entries are utilized
52	per layer for attention calculation. We observe that during the decoding of a long-context request,
53	only a negligible portion of the prefix KV cache is actually accessed. However, the entire prefix KV
54	cache must still be fetched into local memory. To prevent local memory capacity from limiting the
55	request batch size, TB-level memory is required to maintain high concurrency in sparse attention
56	model serving, resulting in high infrastructure costs and poor memory efficiency.
57	An intuitive approach to solve the issue is to transmit only the top-k KV cache entries on demand,
58	which would reduce transmission pressure and conserve local memory. However, this strategy
59	is infeasible for RDMA-based disaggregated systems. First, the top- k indices are dynamically
60	determined per layer at runtime based on the current query vector. The process of fetching the top-k
61	KV is highly latency-sensitive, and the inherent access latency of RDMA cannot meet the strict
62	timing requirement [10]. Second, the sparse top-k KV entries consist of discrete, small data segments.
63	Fetching these data via RDMA requires dozens of independent requests or complex gather/scatter
64	operations, which incur significant software stack overhead [11].
65	Fortunately, the emergingCompute Express Link (CXL)technology [ 12] introduces new opportu-
66	nities for disaggregated KV cache systems in sparse attention models. CXL is built on PCIe physical
67	layer with a streamlined protocol stack, offering significantly lower latency than RDMA. Moreover,
68	CXL supports load/store semantics at cache-line granularity with zero message protocol overhead,
69	making it uniquely suited for reading sparse and fine-grained data. Leveraging these features, we
70	explore the feasibility of using CXL-based disaggregated memory to overcome the limitations of
71	RDMA in sparse attention model serving.
72	We presentSAC(Sparse Attention on CXL), which stores the KV cache in disaggregated CXL
73	memory accessible to multiple servers. Due to its near-DRAM access latency and support for fine-
74	grained load/store semantics, SAC enables the real-time fetching of top-k KV entries during sparse
75	attention calculations without significantly compromising serving performance. By transferring only
76	the required top-k entries on demand, SAC eliminates the transmission bottleneck (P1). Furthermore,
77	because the full KV cache resides in the disaggregated CXL pool at all times, local memory is freed
78	from maintaining redundant data, thereby resolving the local memory wasting problem (P2).

Abstract
The scaling of LLMs toward long-context inference has shifted the primary serving
system bottleneck from computation to memory capacity. Traditional solutions
for dense attention models rely on RDMA-based disaggregated memory pools,
which perform coarse-grained fetching of the entire prefix KV cache from remote

KV entries are active during decoding, these systems still fetch the full KV cache
locally, leading to severe transmission bottlenecks and local memory wastage. To
address this, we propose SAC, the first efficient disaggregated KV cache system
optimized for sparse attention models. By leveraging the low-latency, cache-line
granularity load/store semantics of Compute Express Link (CXL), SAC fetches

The rapid scaling of LLM parameters and the growing demand for long-context inference shift
the bottleneck from computation to memory, where prefix KV cache management has become a
critical challenge in LLM serving [1]. As local GPU HBM and DRAM fall short of the TB-level
requirements of KV cache capacity, RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems emerge as the
standard solution for memory expansion and cross-node sharing [2–4].
In RDMA-based disaggregated systems, RDMA NICs prefetch the entire prefix KV cache into local
memory to ensure low-latency access during the subsequent decoding stages of the request. Although
this full fetching strategy is optimal fordense attentionmodels, it becomes fundamentally inefficient
for the emerging generation ofsparse attentionmodels, such as DeepSeek-V3.2 [ 5], GLM-5.1 [6]
and DeepSeek-V4 [7]. The core problem is that only a small fraction of KV entries are active at any
decoding step, while the KV cache for the full context must be fetched and remain in local memory
during the request. We find that the KV cache full fetching approach directly impacts the efficiency
of disaggregated serving systems for sparse attention models due to two primary problems.

serving throughput of sparse attention models is typically bounded by the achievable batch size,
rather than the compute capacity [8]. For long-context requests, KV cache size can reach dozens of
GBs [9]. Maintaining high concurrency in sparse attention serving places substantial pressure on KV
cache transmission, including RDMA transfers and memory layout rearrangement, which can cause
long queuing delays and degrade time to first token and overall throughput.

which would reduce transmission pressure and conserve local memory. However, this strategy
is infeasible for RDMA-based disaggregated systems. First, the top- k indices are dynamically
determined per layer at runtime based on the current query vector. The process of fetching the top-k
KV is highly latency-sensitive, and the inherent access latency of RDMA cannot meet the strict

operations, which incur significant software stack overhead [11].
